usbControl.other: If you see "USB controlled by", choose "This device".

buildNumber.pixel: Settings › About phone (or About tablet) › Build number
buildNumber.samsung: Settings › About phone (or About tablet) › Software information › Build number
buildNumber.xiaomi: Settings › About phone (or About tablet) › OS version (on older devices: MIUI version)
buildNumber.oneplus: Settings › About device › Version › Build number
buildNumber.motorola: Settings › About phone (or About tablet) › Build number
buildNumber.other: Settings › About phone (or About tablet) › Build number (sometimes inside "Software information")

devOptions.samsung: Settings › Developer options (at the very bottom of Settings)
devOptions.oneplus: Settings › System settings › Developer options (OnePlus: Settings › System › Developer options)

devopts.title: Turn on Developer options
lines: On your device, open {buildNumber}.
Tap the build number 7 times in a row. Enter your PIN if asked.
You'll see "You are now a developer!" (or "Developer mode has been turned on").
Already done this before? Just continue.
devopts.tip: Can't find it? Search Settings for "Build number".

wireless.title: Turn on Wireless debugging
lines: Make sure your device is on the same Wi-Fi as the Frame: {ssid}.
Open {devOptions}.
Scroll down and turn on Wireless debugging.
If asked "Allow wireless debugging on this network?", tick "Always allow on this network" and tap Allow.
wireless.tip: We'll find your device automatically as soon as Wireless debugging is on.
help: Is the device on the same Wi-Fi as the Frame ({ssid})? Guest networks usually block this.
Some routers isolate devices from each other ("AP isolation" or "client isolation"). Turn it off, or use the cable option below.
Wireless debugging turns itself off when the device changes Wi-Fi. Turn it off and on again.
No Wireless debugging option? Your device runs Android 10 or older: use the cable option.

pick_phone.title: Which one is your device?
lines: We found more than one device with Wireless debugging on.
On your device, the Wireless debugging screen shows "IP address & Port". Pick the matching address.

pair_open.title: Open the pairing code
lines: On your device, go to {devOptions}.
Scroll down and tap the words "Wireless debugging" (not the switch) to open its settings.
Tap "Pair device with pairing code".
Keep that window open and the device unlocked.
pair_open.tip: Don't use "Pair device with QR code". The device's camera can't see inside the headset.
help: Keep the device's screen on. Locking it closes the pairing window.
Make sure you tapped "Pair device with pairing code", not the QR code option.

pair_code.title: Enter the pairing code
lines: Your device shows a 6-digit "Wi-Fi pairing code".
Type it on the keypad. After pairing, your device lists the Frame as "scrcpy4Frame@SteamFrame" under Paired devices.

manual.title: Enter the details by hand
lines: On the device's Wireless debugging screen, note the IP address and the port ("IP address & Port").
Then tap "Pair device with pairing code" and note that window's port and 6-digit code. This port is different from the first one.

connecting.title: Connecting
lines: Hang on while we connect to your device.

oem_input.title: Allow touch control
lines: Your device needs one more developer setting before the Frame can control it.
{oemInputLine}
We'll notice as soon as it's on.

oemInputLine.xiaomi: Open {devOptions} and turn on "USB debugging (Security settings)". Xiaomi may ask you to sign in to a Mi account.
oemInputLine.oneplus: Open {devOptions} and turn on "Disable permission monitoring".
oemInputLine.other: Open {devOptions} and look for "USB debugging (Security settings)" or "Disable permission monitoring", and turn it on.

companion.title: Add the companion app? (optional)
lines: The scrcpy4Frame companion is a small app we can install on your device for you. You won't need to tap anything on the device.
Reconnects automatically: it turns Wireless debugging on when you open scrcpy4Frame, and off again when you close it.
Notifications in the headset: your device's notifications pop up on the Frame while scrcpy4Frame is running.
We give it two permissions over the debugging connection: "modify secure settings" (only used for Wireless debugging) and notification access. Uninstall it any time from Settings.

tile.title: Add a Wireless debugging shortcut
lines: Wireless debugging turns itself off when your device restarts or changes Wi-Fi.
We can add a "Wireless debugging" button to your device's Quick Settings, so turning it back on is one tap.

tile_manual.title: Add the shortcut by hand
lines: Your device didn't accept the shortcut automatically.
Open {devOptions} › Quick settings developer tiles.
Turn on "Wireless debugging".
Pull down Quick Settings, tap the pencil icon and drag the tile to the first page.

test.title: You're all set
lines: Point and click to tap. Use the stick to scroll. Right-click (B) means Back.
To disconnect, press Disconnect in scrcpy4Frame, or the Steam Input shortcut for Alt+Q in the mirror window.
Next time, just open scrcpy4Frame and press Connect.

usb_setup.title: Turn on USB debugging
lines: On your device, open {buildNumber} and tap it 7 times to turn on Developer options.
Open {devOptions} and turn on USB debugging.
Have a USB-C data cable ready. Charge-only cables won't work.

usb_plug.title: Plug your device into the Frame
lines: Connect the device to the Frame's USB-C port.
On the device, pull down notifications and tap the USB notification. {usbControl} Do this each time you plug it in.
If the device asks what the USB connection is for, choose "File transfer".
help: Tap the device's USB notification. {usbControl} It goes back to the default each time the cable is plugged in.
Try another cable. Many cables only charge.
On the device, pull down notifications, tap the USB notification and choose "File transfer".
Turn USB debugging off and on again in Developer options.

usb_auth.title: Allow USB debugging
lines: Your device is asking "Allow USB debugging?"
Tick "Always allow from this computer" and tap Allow.

usb_perms.title: One-time permission on the Frame
lines: SteamOS doesn't yet let apps talk to Android devices over USB.
Switch the Frame to Desktop Mode, open Konsole and run the command below once. It needs your password.
Then come back here and plug the device in again.
usb_perms.command: echo 'SUBSYSTEM=="usb", ENV{ID_USB_INTERFACES}=="*:ff4201:*", TAG+="uaccess"' | sudo tee /etc/udev/rules.d/51-scrcpy4frame-adb.rules && sudo udevadm control --reload && sudo udevadm trigger

usb_pick.title: Which device?
lines: Pick the device to set up, or plug in the one you want.

reenable.title: Turn Wireless debugging back on
lines: Pull down Quick Settings on your device and tap "Wireless debugging".
No tile? Open {devOptions} and turn on Wireless debugging.
Make sure the device is on {ssid}.
